storage.scope: Same-runner, same-compiler comparison of joined key/value storage with the original independent allocations. The old builder bodies are an explicit measurement fixture; numeric callback and sorting code stay unchanged. All variants retain checked arithmetic, ownership and cleanup. Twenty-four fresh processes per variant rotate order; each position occurs six times. Full work constructs 500,000 entries and makes 2,000,000 lookups; separate construction programs only print size. Neither is an isolated sort/lookup measurement. Separate instrumented programs count managed requests, retains and charged storage; they are excluded from ordinary timing. Actual timed binaries, sources, counters and raw samples are retained. No C/Rust parity or particular cache/TLB mechanism is claimed.

phases.scope: Separate diagnostic executables compare joined and original separate storage on the same host. Construction-only probes record six phases and allocation addresses for both layouts, so an unreproduced slow control cannot establish a repair. Full-work probes time the actual table construction and subsequent query loop separately, without changing evaluation order. The maintained program constructs its table before printing its size and starting queries; the probe verifies exactly one construction before the query interval and none inside it. No subtraction of independently run programs is used. Clock reads and diagnostic code perturb execution; ordinary timings remain in the storage report. Sixteen fresh processes per variant rotate order. Compare CPU models explicitly across runs.
